o.text: From Proto-Turkic *sal- (“to put, throw, drop, lower”).

From Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (yipek), from Proto-Turkic *yïpak (“silk”), probably a derivation of Proto-Turkic *yip (“thread”). Cognate with Turkish ipek, Turkmen ýüpek, Uzbek ipak, Kazakh жібек (jibek), Kyrgyz жибек (jibek).
From gəzmək + -əyən. Cognate with Turkish gezegen.
Borrowed from Classical Persian آیَتُاللّٰه (āyatu-l-lāh), from Arabic آيَةُ ٱللَّٰهِ (ʔāyatu llāhi, “sign of God”), from آيَة (ʔāya, “sign”) + اللّٰه (allāh, “God”).
Borrowed from Arabic عددي. By surface analysis, ədəd + -i.
